Q2_QRE2_P34_01_domainSide.verdict: Acceptable in domain terms: the rule, the question order and the re-ask after a confirmation sent first.
Q2_QRE2_P34_01_domainSide.order: The start time comes first because rule 0.8 makes it the deciding fact. A strength session on the first day cannot be ordered without it, and the two readings give different states. The I6 confirmation reads the whole record, so asked first it could not settle that state. After the restatement, I6 is asked only when the state the return started from changes, that is, only when the late fact is genuine late evidence (Founder 0.7, CF-P34-04). On the candidate: RS1 (start after the lift) gives the I6 question (interruption.episodeId for the trip), then the confirmation gives REESTABLISH, and later reviews give KEEP, ADOPT_LOGGED_LOADS, KEEP. The plan equals the control with the start time stated from the outset (RS1c, T33): back-squat 1x9, db lifts 1x8 ESTABLISH, against 1x7 and 1x12 before the lift was known. RS2 (start before the lift) gives KEEP with the plan unchanged, because nothing is left to confirm. This asks only what changes the decision and keeps confirmation-first wherever late evidence changes the state. Compared with the all-facts-known reading (RS1k: the lift reported with the holiday from the outset), RS1 lets Sunday's long run wait and re-establishes the dumbbell loads instead of reading them from the log. Both differences are conservative and come from the existing late-evidence path and the day of the decision; RS1 equals RS1c, which goes through the same path.
Q2_QRE2_P34_01_domainSide.confirmFirst: Acceptable. RS3: confirming the trip first asks the start time again, because the deciding fact is still unstated. The confirmation is kept, and the restatement then applies the return by itself: one question per missing fact, never a second confirmation, no later ask, and the same plan as RS1. Sent as a declaration, the restatement is recorded and the next return report or weekly review applies it (T33). While the start time is unanswered (RS6), the ask lasts for the rest of the re-entry week. Week 7 then reads the late fact as every late fact is read (GATED_NEXT_STEP, KEEP), and the plan in force keeps the conservative default reading (the session after the start). This is I6 as designed.
Q2_QRE2_P34_01_domainSide.rule: Right. A report that names a break the latest return listed and repeats every fact of it, apart from the name and a start time on its first day, is the same episode stated more finely, not a break of its own. Reading it as a new break would count the same days twice (restatedKeep's counterfactual). 'The newest report decides' is I1/I3 (a newer report of the same named interruption replaces only the report in force). It is not last-write-wins between unrelated reports, which Phase 3.2 forbids: the identity is explicit. Any other changed fact is not consumed and is asked (O-02), which fails closed: nothing is applied and no dose is raised. Probed edges: (a) a named report that changes the holiday's reason to an injury (RS4, by a weekly review and by a return report) routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, and the next review stays clinical, on all three runtimes, so clinical first and R-F08-1 are untouched; (b) a changed last day (RS5) is asked; (c) a restatement followed by a newer report changing the last day (RS7) is asked, so the newest decides; (d) a changed last day followed by the restatement (RS5x) resolves through I6 to REESTABLISH with no later ask on the candidate, where 46934a0 and R7D-FREEZE-4 stay in ASK through week 8. The O-02 wording is observation SSCTR-P35-O03.
Q2_QRE2_P34_01_domainSide.cfP3402: The correction path (R04) equals the correction with the start time stated from the outset, by every channel, idempotently (T33; it passes on my rebuild). That is CF-P34-02's equivalence on this path.

Q4_HARNESS7.verdict: P18(c), P18(f) and the P17/P08 restatement reading read the binding texts correctly. P18(e) mostly does, with one exception: it is not wholly inside the runtime's systemic rule (finding SSCTR-P35-F01, an instrument issue, non-blocking for the freeze and binding before any final holdout).
Q4_HARNESS7.P18c: Correct. The reducer's systemic rule reads every session's latest report, counted or optional, and holds every gate (BR-Q3.2(1); BR-Q4.2: an optional session counts only through that rule). mayConverge counts any live session whose report the runtime may read as adverse: UNDER, ADVERSE, HARDER or IMPAIRED, which also covers what the classifier calls CONFLICTING. It also counts a recorded SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL. That is a superset of the rule, so P18(c) never reads as nominal a week the systemic rule may hold, and it stays sufficient (stricter, as Δ3 registered). On my candidate run of the recheck2 detectors, SY1's week is no longer read as nominal, which removes the DEV-48 false block. P18(c) still never reads a week with an adverse required session as nominal, because executedNominal requires nominal responses (BR-Q6 per session).
Q4_HARNESS7.P18e: Mostly right: no sport re-enters, by TRAINING_AFTER or OWN_RETURN, through a week whose reports converge adversely (BR-Q3.2(1), BR-Q6). It excludes partial reports, as kindOf does. The exception: it counts every complete report with recovery ADVERSE. The reducer's classifier (r6-learning classify) reads performance OVER with recovery ADVERSE (or with effort HARDER) as CONFLICTING, not ADVERSE, unless the report is confounded. The systemic rule counts ADVERSE rows only, and BR-Q6 binds it unchanged. Probe SYc1 (SY1 with those responses on the strength session and the optional shakeout): the candidate gives TRAINING_AFTER, reentry 2026-12-21, conformant with BR-Q4.2-4.3 and BR-Q6 as the reducer reads them, while adverseConvergence(week 7) is true, so P18(e) would report SYSTEMIC_WEEK_REENTERED (SAFETY_BLOCKER). The same corner reaches ordinary weeks: a CONFLICTING strength session advances, while a recovery-ADVERSE run in the other sport is one session in one sport, so it is not systemic. The DEV corpus has no such response, so validation 7 cannot see it. Controls: SYc0 (recovery ADVERSE only) gives the hold and P18(e) is true; SYc2 (next day IMPAIRED) gives the hold and P18(e) is false (necessary only, as intended).
Q4_HARNESS7.P18f: Correct. It applies R7-C G01 (unknown training is neither done nor not done, so it is asked) and the F02 closure. For every applied return with separate breaks, including corrections and confirmations, a break placed by the training after it (OWN_RETURN, TRAINING_NOT_REESTABLISHED, NO_TRAINING_BETWEEN) has no live planned session without a report before the next break, or before the stop for OWN_RETURN. Days inside another episode's in-force recorded stop are known; the superseded report of the same episode is not. TRAINING_AFTER rows are left out, as the runtime asks nothing after a full re-entry week. That matches stopOf.
Q4_HARNESS7.P17P08: Correct against INTERFACE-7 section 2: a restatement is that break's report, never a break of its own, so it opens no P17 window and P08 measures no return from it. A changed fact still opens its window (W-P17e), and a later report of any kind still ends an earlier window. restatesListed matches the runtime's restates in substance: the same name match, the same comparison of every fact but the name and start time, and the start time absent or on the first day. It differs in two respects, both harmless. It exempts any restating review, not only the newest; a newer report that changes a fact still opens its own window. It also does not check that the start time is no later than the report, which cannot happen for an earlier break a return already listed. For BR-Q3.2(1), BR-Q4.2 and BR-Q6, see P18(c) and P18(e) above.

Q5_newNumbers.reasoning: The added runtime code holds only existing day and index arithmetic (onDate(x,+1/-1), x.j+1, .at(-1)), the existing timezone default (??0) and the structural rows.length<2: a listing needs an earlier break beside LATEST, which is no training quantity. Other digits appear only in comments and ids (rule 0.8, Phase 3.4/3.5, finding ids). Policy, catalog, composition and the r5/r6/r7-b0 inputs are unchanged since 46934a0. The harness's '>1 sport or >=3 sessions' copies the reducer's existing systemic rule. Neither this record's finding nor its proposed O-P35-01 reading needs a number.

findings.severity: MODERATE (validity of the final holdout; no product-safety effect, the runtime is conformant)
findings.finding: Δ27 registers P18(e) as 'a reading inside the systemic rule, therefore a necessary condition', and the code comment says the runtime reads every report it counts as adverse. That is not so for a complete report with recovery ADVERSE and performance OVER (or effort HARDER with performance OVER). The reducer's classifier reads it CONFLICTING, not ADVERSE, unless the report is confounded. The systemic rule, bound unchanged by BR-Q6, counts ADVERSE rows only. P18(e) can therefore report SYSTEMIC_WEEK_REENTERED (SAFETY_BLOCKER) for a runtime that follows the binding rule. On the final holdout that would be a false blocker, which closes R7-D NOT_READY with no correction loop.

observations.note: O-P35-01, classified as a disclosed residual (Q3). The Δ31 text and the freeze record should say: identical on R7D-FREEZE-4, 46934a0 and the candidate for single-break corrections (MS); in the two-break correction shape of T32 (MV), R7D-FREEZE-4 eased the next quality slot, because its correction dropped the earlier break, and 46934a0 and the candidate do not. On that shape it is one eased quality session less conservative than R7D-FREEZE-4, from Phase 3.4. Route the R27 / R7-A.2 slot reading (Q3) to the next Founder-authorized phase. The final holdout's domain judge reads this shape as the disclosed residual.

This is a precision point in the role's own BR-Q6 text, not a defect. BR-Q6's second sentence ('an adverse or conflicting response on a required session makes its sport not re-entry-complete') matches the run gates, which hold on ADVERSE or CONFLICTING. The strength gate holds on ADVERSE only: a CONFLICTING strength session whose logged target is met advances, in ordinary weeks as in re-entry weeks (SYc1: TRAINING_AFTER). BR-Q4.3 binds complete(STRENGTH), and BR-Q6's first sentence binds the gates unchanged, so the runtime is conformant, as on 46934a0. Read the second sentence as 'as the reducer's gates read it' and disclose it. Whether a strength session above target with an adverse recovery should hold is an R6 gate question, not reviewed here.

When a named report of an earlier listed break changes a fact other than the start time (RS5, RS7), O-02 asks it with the pre-existing text 'say when it started and ended, as one period'. For breaks with weeks of training between, that wording invites the athlete to merge them, a reading direction A forbids (weeks of training between are never days of the stop). It fails closed, it is identical on 46934a0, and R7D-FREEZE-4 asks a relation question there. The candidate also adds an exit, because restating the break resolves it (RS5x). For the interface and wording owner: name the fact actually needed, either the break as first reported (with its start time if asked) or the change confirmed. No domain effect beyond the ask.

aeReview.1_planAdequate: Yes on the closure shapes. SY1 holds running under the systemic rule. CU3, CU1, LC1 and CU2 ask about the uncovered sessions before any return applies, then give the fresh report's return. The restatement gives the reading of the start time stated from the outset. One residual is disclosed: O-P35-01.
aeReview.2_materialFact: Yes. The declared breaks, the executed sessions with their responses, the named correction, the restatement and the late lift are all on the append-only record. The unreported sessions and the start time are facts to ask, not facts on record.
aeReview.3_keepDefensible: KEEP of 8e78b8a as the frozen shadow reference is defensible under the conditions below.
aeReview.4_changeNecessary: No further runtime change before this freeze. One instrument change (SSCTR-P35-F01) is necessary before the holdout.
aeReview.5_smallestIntervention: A one-predicate harness correction (adverseConvergence reads as the reducer's classifier does) with a DEV control, by PREREG addendum.
aeReview.6_smallerAlternatives: Leaving P18(e) as is risks a false SAFETY_BLOCKER on the holdout. Listing the shape as NOT_EVALUABLE is the acceptable smaller fallback. Changing the runtime's systemic rule instead would change a binding rule (BR-Q6) and is out of scope.
aeReview.7_priorityAndProgression: The closures restore BR-Q3.2's coupling and the correction rule and raise no dose. O-P35-01 leaves one quality session un-eased, at no dose above the last executed one.
aeReview.8_evidenceSupportsDose: No dose is judged here. The approved R6 recipes, the decision's CL1-CL7 and R27's recorded weight are relied on as recorded.
aeReview.9_uncertainty: How often these shapes occur in real use: a correction that moves a short break over its eased slot is plausible but uncommon; a report with performance OVER and an adverse recovery is plausible. Group means only; no individual prediction.
aeReview.10_askHoldClinical: ASK for the uncovered sessions (F02) and for the start time (rule 0.8), with I6 confirmation-first when the state changes. The systemic hold for F01. CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for a clinical change, even when the report names an earlier break (RS4). F08 stays BLOCKED_BY_AUTHORITY.
